paraphrase: Chapter 4 moves in six steps. (1) 4.1–3: the Lord declares that he taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvat, who passed it to Manu and Ikṣvāku; known by the royal sages through succession, it was lost over time, and he now teaches it again to Arjuna as his devotee and friend. (2) 4.4–10: to Arjuna's question how he could have taught it before Vivasvat, the Lord answers that he knows his many births; unborn and lord of beings, he comes into being by his own māyā whenever dharma declines, to protect the good, destroy wrongdoers and establish dharma; whoever knows his divine birth and action is not reborn and comes to him, as many have, purified by knowledge. (3) 4.11–15: he receives people as they approach him; result-seekers worship the gods; he made the four classes by guṇa and action yet is a non-doer, unstained by action; knowing this, the ancients acted, so Arjuna should act. (4) 4.16–23: what action, wrong action and inaction are; the wise see inaction in action; the one free of desire, whose actions are burnt in the fire of knowledge, is not bound though acting. (5) 4.24–32: action as sacrifice — Brahman is every element of the offering — and a list of the many kinds of sacrifice (to the gods, of the senses, of breath, of things, of austerity, of study and knowledge), all born of action. (6) 4.33–42: the sacrifice of knowledge is best, all action culminating in knowledge; knowledge is to be learned from seers of truth by prostration, questioning and service; it is a raft over all wrong, a fire burning all action, the supreme purifier, won by the faithful and self-restrained and bringing peace, while the doubter perishes; the chapter ends: cut doubt with the sword of knowledge, resort to yoga and stand up. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to establish the ancient authority of the teaching and the Lord who gives it, and to show that action done as sacrifice, without attachment, culminates in knowledge, so that Arjuna may act free of doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa (with Arjuna's questions)
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter colophons are not in this edition's segments; the vulgate colophon title is 'Jñāna-karma-saṃnyāsa-yoga'. Speaker: Kṛṣṇa throughout except Arjuna's question at 4.4.

paraphrase: Therefore, cutting with the sword of knowledge (jñānāsi) this doubt of yours, born of ignorance (ajñāna) and lodged in the heart, resort to yoga; stand up, O Bhārata.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

notes: The chapter closes by returning to the battlefield situation: 'uttiṣṭha' (stand up) is the call to act.

paraphrase: Chapter 5 moves in five steps. (1) 5.1–6: Arjuna asks which is better, the renunciation of actions or yoga; the Lord answers that both lead to the highest good but the yoga of action is superior; the constant renunciant is the one without aversion or desire; only the childish call Sāṃkhya and Yoga separate, since both reach the same place; renunciation is hard without yoga. (2) 5.7–12: the one yoked in yoga is not stained though acting; the knower of reality thinks 'I do nothing', holding that the senses move among their objects; acting with actions placed in Brahman and without attachment, one is unstained like a lotus leaf; yogins act for self-purification; abandoning the fruit brings peace, attachment to it binds. (3) 5.13–17: the embodied one, having renounced all actions mentally, sits in the city of nine gates neither acting nor causing action; the master creates neither agency nor actions nor their fruit — nature acts; knowledge is covered by ignorance, and when ignorance is destroyed knowledge shines like the sun and those intent on That reach non-return. (4) 5.18–26: the wise see the same in all beings; those established in sameness are established in Brahman, which is flawless and the same; unmoved by pleasant and unpleasant, finding happiness within rather than in contact-born pleasures, withstanding desire and anger, having happiness, delight and light within, the yogin becomes Brahman and attains brahma-nirvāṇa, which surrounds the self-knowing ascetics. (5) 5.27–29: an outline of meditation (external contacts put outside, gaze between the brows, prāṇa and apāna made equal) for the sage intent on liberation, who is ever free; and the closing: knowing the Lord as enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, great lord of all worlds and friend of all beings, one attains peace. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to answer the question of renunciation versus action by showing that true renunciation is inner and that yoga leads to the same goal, the peace of brahma-nirvāṇa.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa (with Arjuna's questions)
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter colophons are not in this edition's segments; the vulgate colophon title is 'Karma-saṃnyāsa-yoga'. Speaker: Kṛṣṇa throughout except Arjuna's question at 5.1.

original.text:

kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ

original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

labhante brahmanirvāṇamṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ|
chinnadvaidhā yatātmānaḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām|
abhito brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate viditātmanām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For ascetics (yati) free from desire and anger, whose minds are restrained and who know the self (viditātman), brahma-nirvāṇa is present all around (abhitaḥ).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
sparśānkṛtvā bahirbāhyāṃścakṣuścaivāntare bhruvoḥ|
prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Putting the external contacts outside, and the gaze (cakṣus) between the brows (antare bhruvoḥ), making equal (sama) the prāṇa and apāna that move within the nostrils,
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: One sentence runs through 5.27–28. The method is given only in outline; the fuller instruction on meditation follows in 6.10–28.

original.text:
yatendriyamanobuddhirmunirmokṣaparāyaṇaḥ|
vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: the sage (muni) whose senses, mind and intellect are restrained, who has liberation (mokṣa) as the highest goal, from whom desire (icchā), fear and anger are gone — he is liberated forever (sadā mukta eva).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram|
suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā māṃ śāntimṛcchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Knowing me as the enjoyer (bhoktṛ) of sacrifices and austerities, the great lord of all the worlds (sarva-loka-maheśvara), the friend (suhṛd) of all beings, one attains peace (śānti).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

paraphrase: Chapter 6 moves in eight steps. (1) 6.1–4: the one who does the required action without depending on its fruit is both renunciant and yogin; renunciation is yoga, for no one is a yogin without renouncing intention; for one ascending to yoga action is the means, for one who has ascended calm is the means. (2) 6.5–9: one should raise the self by the self, which is its own friend or enemy; the conquered, calm self is composed amid the opposites; the yoked yogin sees clod, stone and gold alike and regards friend and foe, good and wicked with an equal mind. (3) 6.10–17: the practice of meditation — solitude, a clean place and a firm seat, one-pointed mind, body, head and neck in line, gaze at the nose-tip, fearlessness, the vow of the brahmacārin, the mind on the Lord — bringing peace that culminates in nirvāṇa; and moderation in food, recreation, effort, sleep and waking. (4) 6.18–28: the yoked mind is like a lamp in a windless place; the state where the stilled mind rests and the self sees the self, knowing boundless happiness beyond the senses and unshaken by sorrow, is called yoga, the disconnection from union with suffering; the method of gradually stilling the mind and bringing it back whenever it wanders; the calmed yogin attains the highest happiness, contact with Brahman. (5) 6.29–32: the yoked one sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self; whoever sees the Lord everywhere is never lost to him; the highest yogin sees pleasure and pain everywhere by likeness to himself. (6) 6.33–36: Arjuna objects that the mind is too restless for such sameness; the Lord grants this but says it is held by practice and dispassion, and yoga is attainable by the self-controlled through right means. (7) 6.37–45: Arjuna asks the fate of the faithful one who falls from yoga; the Lord answers that no doer of good is lost: he dwells in the worlds of the meritorious, is reborn among the pure and prosperous or among yogins, regains his former understanding, is carried by former practice, and, perfected over many births, reaches the highest goal. (8) 6.46–47: the yogin surpasses ascetics, knowers and ritualists, so Arjuna should be a yogin; of all yogins the one who worships the Lord with faith, his inner self gone into him, is the most yoked. Purpose, as the chapter presents it: to set out the discipline of meditation and its fruit, to reassure the practitioner about restlessness and failure, and to place devotion to the Lord at the summit of yoga.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa (with Arjuna's questions)
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Chapter colophons are not in this edition's segments; vulgate colophon titles are 'Dhyāna-yoga' or 'Ātma-saṃyama-yoga'. Speaker: Kṛṣṇa, with Arjuna at 6.33–34 and 6.37–39.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ|
sa saṃnyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnirna cākriyaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: One who does the action that is to be done (kārya karma) without depending on the fruit of action is a renunciant (saṃnyāsin) and a yogin — not the one without the sacred fire (niragni), nor the one without rites (akriya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'niragni' (one who has given up the ritual fires) and 'akriya' (one who has given up rites/activity) name the outward marks of formal renunciation, which the verse says do not by themselves make the renunciant.

original.text:
yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava|
na hyasaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Know that what they call renunciation (saṃnyāsa) is yoga; for no one becomes a yogin without renouncing intention (saṅkalpa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ārurukṣormuneryogaṃ karma kāraṇamucyate|
yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇamucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For the sage (muni) who wishes to ascend to yoga (ārurukṣu), action is said to be the means (kāraṇa); for the same one, once he has ascended to yoga (yogārūḍha), calm (śama) is said to be the means.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Two stages of one practitioner, each with its own means: action for the one ascending, calm for the one who has ascended.

original.text:
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasvanuṣajjate|
sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhastadocyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: When one is not attached to the objects of the senses nor to actions, and has renounced all intentions (sarva-saṅkalpa-saṃnyāsin), then one is said to have ascended to yoga (yogārūḍha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
uddharedātmanā''tmānaṃ nātmānamavasādayet|
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: One should raise the self by the self (uddhared ātmanātmānam) and not let the self sink; for the self alone is the self's friend (bandhu), and the self alone is the self's enemy (ripu).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'ātman' here spans the person, the mind and the self; the verse plays on the word. Commentators commonly read 'by the self' as by the (discriminating) mind.

original.text:
bandhurātmā''tmanastasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ|
anātmanastu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The self is the friend of that self by whom the self itself has been conquered; but for one who is not self-possessed (anātman), the self itself would act with hostility, like an enemy.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ|
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāpamānayoḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For one who has conquered the self and is at peace (praśānta), the supreme self (paramātman) is composed (samāhita) amid cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The construal is disputed: 'paramātmā samāhitaḥ' may mean that the supreme Self is present/realized as his self, or (reading 'param' adverbially) that his self is supremely composed; commentators divide.

original.text:
jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ|
yukta ityucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The yogin whose self is satisfied with knowledge (jñāna) and realized knowledge (vijñāna), who stands unmoved (kūṭastha), whose senses are conquered, to whom a clod, a stone and gold are the same, is called 'yoked' (yukta).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'kūṭastha' — literally 'standing on the peak' or 'like an anvil'; i.e. unmoved.

original.text:
suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu|
sādhuṣvapi ca pāpeṣu samabuddhirviśiṣyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: One who has an equal mind (sama-buddhi) toward well-wishers, friends, foes, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful and kinsmen, and toward the good (sādhu) and the wicked alike, excels.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yogī yuñjīta satatamātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ|
ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīraparigrahaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The yogin should constantly yoke himself (ātmānam, the self/mind), remaining in a secluded place (rahasi), alone, with mind and self restrained, without expectations (nirāśīḥ) and without possessions (aparigraha).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiramāsanamātmanaḥ|
nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ cailājinakuśottaram
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: In a clean place (śuci deśa), setting up for himself a firm seat (āsana), neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass,
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: One instruction runs from 6.10 to 6.14. The order of cloth, deerskin and kuśa grass in 'cailājinakuśottaram' is read in different ways (which is laid over which).

original.text:
tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ|
upaviśyāsane yuñjyādyogamātmaviśuddhaye
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: there, making the mind one-pointed (ekāgra), with the activities of mind (citta) and senses restrained, sitting on the seat he should practise yoga for the purification of the self (ātma-viśuddhi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayannacalaṃ sthiraḥ|
saṃprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ diśaścānavalokayan
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: holding body, head and neck in line (sama) and motionless, steady, gazing at the tip of his own nose (nāsikāgra) and not looking about in the directions,
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Some commentators (e.g. Śaṅkara) take 'saṃprekṣya' as 'as if gazing', i.e. the eyes resting toward the nose-tip while attention is held within, rather than a fixed stare.

original.text:
praśāntātmā vigatabhīrbrahmacārivrate sthitaḥ|
manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: calm in self (praśāntātmā), free from fear (vigatabhīḥ), firm in the vow of the brahmacārin (brahmacāri-vrata), restraining the mind, with thought on me (maccitta), yoked, he should sit intent on me (matpara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'brahmacāri-vrata' — the observance of the Vedic student, which commentators gloss as celibacy together with the student's other restraints. The object of meditation is given as 'me' (the Lord).

original.text:
yuñjannevaṃ sadā''tmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ|
śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthāmadhigacchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Thus always yoking himself, the yogin with controlled mind attains the peace (śānti) that culminates in nirvāṇa (nirvāṇa-paramā) and abides in me (matsaṃsthā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
nātyaśnatastu yogo'sti na caikāntamanaśnataḥ|
na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Yoga is not for one who eats too much, nor for one who does not eat at all, nor for one given to too much sleep, nor for one who stays awake too long.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The text's own warning against both over-indulgence and total abstention from food and sleep.

original.text:
yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu|
yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For one who is measured (yukta) in food and recreation (āhāra-vihāra), measured in exertion in actions, measured in sleep and waking, yoga becomes the destroyer of suffering (duḥkhahā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yadā viniyataṃ cittamātmanyevāvatiṣṭhate|
niḥspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ityucyate tadā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: When the well-restrained mind (citta) rests in the self alone, free of craving (niḥspṛha) for all objects of desire, then one is called 'yoked' (yukta).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā|
yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogamātmanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: 'As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker' — that is the simile handed down (smṛtā) for the yogin of restrained mind (citta) who practises the yoga of the self.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā|
yatra caivātmanā''tmānaṃ paśyannātmani tuṣyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Where the mind (citta), stilled (niruddha) by the practice of yoga (yoga-sevā), comes to rest (uparamate), and where, seeing the self by the self, one is content in the self;
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: One sentence runs through 6.20–23 ('where … that should be known as yoga'). The vocabulary of the stilled mind (niruddha citta) parallels Yoga Sūtra 1.2.

original.text:
sukhamātyantikaṃ yattadbuddhigrāhyamatīndriyam|
vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaścalati tattvataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: where one knows that boundless (ātyantika) happiness which is grasped by the intellect (buddhi-grāhya) and lies beyond the senses (atīndriya), and established in which one does not waver from the truth (tattvataḥ);
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ|
yasminsthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: having gained which one does not think any other gain greater, and established in which one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow —
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
taṃ vidyād duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam|
sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇṇacetasā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: that should be known as the disconnection from union with suffering (duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyoga), called yoga.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Completes 6.20–22. The definition names yoga by a play on words: it is 'dis-union' (viyoga) from 'union' (saṃyoga) with suffering.

original.text:

sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo'nirviṇṇacetasā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: That yoga should be practised with determination (niścaya) and with an undespondent mind (anirviṇṇa-cetas).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa

original.text:
saṅkalpaprabhavānkāmāṃstyaktvā sarvānaśeṣataḥ|
manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Abandoning without remainder all desires (kāma) that arise from intention (saṅkalpa-prabhava), and restraining the whole troop of the senses on every side by the mind alone,
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: One instruction runs through 6.24–25.

original.text:
śanaiḥ śanairuparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā|
ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcidapi cintayet
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: one should come to rest (uparamet) little by little, by the intellect (buddhi) held in steadfastness (dhṛti); having made the mind abide in the self (ātma-saṃstha), one should think of nothing at all (na kiṃcid api cintayet).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yato yato niścarati manaścañcalamasthiram|
tatastato niyamyaitadātmanyeva vaśaṃ nayet
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whenever the restless (cañcala), unsteady mind wanders off, from there one should restrain it and bring it under control in the self alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
praśāntamanasaṃ hyenaṃ yoginaṃ sukhamuttamam|
upaiti śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtamakalmaṣam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For supreme happiness (sukham uttamam) comes to this yogin whose mind is calmed, whose passion (rajas) is quieted, who has become Brahman (brahmabhūta) and is free of stain (akalmaṣa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'śāntarajasam' — whose rajas is stilled; the verse does not expound the guṇa doctrine here.

original.text:
yuñjannevaṃ sadā''tmānaṃ yogī vigatakalmaṣaḥ|
sukhena brahmasaṃsparśamatyantaṃ sukhamaśnute
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Thus always yoking the self, the yogin freed from stain easily attains the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman (brahma-saṃsparśa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sarvabhūtasthamātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani|
īkṣate yogayuktātmā sarvatra samadarśanaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The one whose self is yoked in yoga, who sees the same everywhere (sarvatra sama-darśana), sees the self as abiding in all beings and all beings in the self.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati|
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Whoever sees me everywhere and sees everything in me — I am not lost to him, and he is not lost to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sarvabhūtasthitaṃ yo māṃ bhajatyekatvamāsthitaḥ|
sarvathā vartamāno'pi sa yogī mayi vartate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The yogin who, established in oneness (ekatva), worships (bhajati) me as abiding in all beings, abides in me however he may be living (sarvathā vartamāno 'pi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'ekatvam āsthitaḥ' — established in oneness (of the Lord in all beings); commentators read it as identity or as unity of worship.

original.text:
ātmaupamyena sarvatra samaṃ paśyati yo'rjuna|
sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ saḥ yogī paramo mataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The one who, by likeness to himself (ātmaupamya), sees the same everywhere, whether pleasure or pain — that yogin is considered the highest (paramo yogī).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Commentators read it as regarding others' pleasure and pain as one's own, or as seeing all selves as alike in nature; both rest on 'by likeness to oneself'.

original.text:
yo'yaṃ yogastvayā proktaḥ sāmyena madhusūdana|
etasyāhaṃ na paśyāmi cañcalatvāt sthitiṃ sthirām
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: This yoga which you have declared as sameness (sāmya), Madhusūdana — because of restlessness (cañcalatva), I do not see its steady standing.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
cañcalaṃ hi manaḥ kṛṣṇa pramāthi balavaddṛḍham|
tasyāhaṃ nigrahaṃ manye vāyoriva suduṣkaram
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: For the mind is restless, Kṛṣṇa, turbulent (pramāthin), strong and obstinate (dṛḍha); I think restraining it (nigraha) is as very hard as restraining the wind.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
asaṃśayaṃ mahābāho mano durnigrahaṃ calaṃ|
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Without doubt the mind is hard to restrain and restless; but it is held (gṛhyate) through practice (abhyāsa) and dispassion (vairāgya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
asaṃyatātmanā yogo duṣprāpa iti me matiḥ|
vaśyātmanā tu yatatā śakyo'vāptumupāyataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Yoga is hard to attain for one whose self is unrestrained — this is my view; but by one whose self is under control and who strives, it can be attained through the right means (upāya).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ayatiḥ śraddhayopeto yogāccalitamānasaḥ|
aprāpya yogasaṃsiddhiṃ kāṃ gatiṃ kṛṣṇa gacchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: One lacking in effort (ayati), though endowed with faith (śraddhā), whose mind has fallen away from yoga — not having reached perfection in yoga (yoga-saṃsiddhi), what course (gati) does he go, Kṛṣṇa?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
kaccinnobhayavibhraṣṭaśchinnābhramiva naśyati|
apratiṣṭho mahābāho vimūḍho brahmaṇaḥ pathi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Fallen from both (ubhaya-vibhraṣṭa), without support (apratiṣṭha), bewildered on the path of Brahman, does he not perish like a scattered cloud?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'Both' is commonly read as both the rewards of works and the goal of yoga; the verse does not specify.

original.text:
etanme saṃśayaṃ kṛṣṇa chettumarhasyaśeṣataḥ|
tvadanyaḥ saṃśayasyāsya chettā na hyupapadyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: You should cut away this doubt of mine completely, Kṛṣṇa; for no one other than you can be found who could cut this doubt.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśastasya vidyate|
nahi kalyāṇakṛtkaśicaddurgatiṃ tāta gacchati
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Neither here nor hereafter is there destruction for him; for no one who does good (kalyāṇa-kṛt), dear friend (tāta), goes to a bad end (durgati).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃ lokānuṣitvā śāśvatīḥ samāḥ|
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe yogabhraṣṭo'bhijāyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Having reached the worlds of those who have done merit (puṇya-kṛt) and dwelt there for countless years, the one fallen from yoga (yoga-bhraṣṭa) is born in the house of the pure and prosperous (śuci, śrīmat).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
athavā yogināmeva kule bhavati dhīmatām|
etaddhi durlabhataraṃ loke janma yadīdṛśam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Or else he is born in the very family of wise yogins; for a birth such as this is harder to obtain in the world.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tatra taṃ buddhisaṃyogaṃ labhate paurvadehikam|
yatate ca tato bhūyaḥ saṃsiddhau kurunandana
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: There he regains the connection with understanding (buddhi-saṃyoga) belonging to his former body (paurvadehika), and from there he strives again (bhūyaḥ) for perfection (saṃsiddhi).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
pūrvābhyāsena tenaiva hriyate hyavaśo'pi saḥ|
jijñāsurapi yogasya śabdabrahmātivartate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: By that same former practice (pūrvābhyāsa) he is carried along even without his will (avaśa); even one who merely wishes to know yoga (jijñāsu) goes beyond the word-Brahman (śabdabrahman).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'śabdabrahman' is taken by commentators as the Veda, i.e. the Vedic works and their rewards; the verse itself says only that the inquirer into yoga passes beyond it.

original.text:
prayatnādyatamānastu yogī saṃśuddhakilbiṣaḥ|
anekajanmasaṃsiddhastato yāti parāṃ gatim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: But the yogin who strives with effort, cleansed of faults (kilbiṣa), perfected through many births (aneka-janma-saṃsiddha), then goes to the highest goal (parā gati).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
tapasvibhyo'dhiko yogī jñānibhyo'pi mato'dhikaḥ|
karmibhyaścādhiko yogī tasmādyogī bhavārjuna
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: The yogin is greater than the ascetics (tapasvin), considered greater even than the knowers (jñānin), and greater than those who perform works (karmin); therefore be a yogin, Arjuna.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'jñānin' here is read by commentators as those with scriptural learning (as distinct from the realized knower of 7.16–18), and 'karmin' as performers of Vedic rites; the verse itself does not specify.

original.text:
yogināmapi sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā|
śraddhāvānbhajate yo māṃ sa me yuktatamo mataḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: And of all yogins, the one who, full of faith (śraddhāvān), worships (bhajate) me with his inner self gone into me (madgatena antarātmanā) — he is considered by me the most yoked (yuktatama).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Closes the chapter and leads into ch. 7 (7.1: 'with mind attached to me, practising yoga, taking refuge in me').
